rounds.text: Shree Hanuman Sugar & Industries Ltd presents an extraordinary statistical anomaly, trading at a price-to-book multiple of just 0.04x against a book value of ₹ 82.1 per share while the stock sits at ₹ 3.47 [E1]. This extreme discount values the entire enterprise at a minuscule market capitalization of ₹ 6.41 Cr [E2], representing a near-complete detachment from the underlying asset base where the price sits at only 1% of its 52-week range [E4]. Underlying fundamentals show powerful recent momentum, evidenced by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 23% [E15] that comfortably outpaces the sector median profit growth of 16.7% [E63]. This performance triggers bullish screening criteria for year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% alongside accelerating earnings growth [E55, E56]. Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded profit growth has declined by -112% [E16], compounded profit growth over 5 years rests at -36% [E14], and the return on equity stands at -0.59% compared to a sector benchmark of 8.5% [E8].

The bear case rests on a fundamentally unprofitable operation that destroys capital, evidenced by a negative return on equity of -0.59% and a negative return on assets of -0.38% [E7, E8]. Long-term wealth creation is non-existent, highlighted by a stagnant 10-year compounded profit growth of just 2% and a severe 5-year contraction of -36% [E13, E14]. This downward trajectory has intensified recently, with trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth collapsing by -112% [E16], proving the business is moving backward. Furthermore, the company returns nothing to its owners, offering a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3], while the stock languishes at the very bottom of its 52-week range at just 1% of the way up [E4]. Conceded: the company displays a 3-year compounded profit growth of 23% alongside accelerating short-term earnings metrics [E15, E55, E56]. However, these isolated green shoots fail to mask a business trading at a negative P/E of -7.31x [E5] where price growth has drastically outpaced underlying fundamental delivery by 77% [E45].

Conceded: negative return on equity of -0.59% and return on assets of -0.38% [E7, E8], along with a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3] and a 5-year profit contraction of -36% [E14]. However, the bear's focus on a 10-year growth rate of 2% [E13] and a trailing twelve-month drop of -112% [E16] ignores the genuine medium-term turnaround visible in a 3-year compounded profit growth of 23% [E15]. This recent acceleration is explicitly backed by screen reasons showing profit growth exceeding 20% YoY and accelerating earnings [E55, E56], outperforming the sector median profit growth of 16.7% [E63]. The claim that the stock languishes at the bottom of its range [E4] overlooks the extreme statistical anomaly of a price-to-book ratio of 0.04x [E1] against a sector benchmark of 1.86x [E6], offering an asset backing that dwarfs the microscopic market capitalisation of ₹ 6.41 Cr [E2]. Finally, the negative P/E of -7.31x [E5] simply reflects the cyclical nature of a business whose underlying profit expansion over the past three years [E15] is being completely unappreciated by the market.

The bull’s reliance on a 3-year profit growth of 23% [E15] is undermined by the most recent performance data, which shows a catastrophic trailing twelve-month profit contraction of -112% [E16], rendering the medium-term trend irrelevant. While the bull cites screen reasons for accelerating earnings [E55, E56], these are contradicted by the actual negative ROA of -0.38% [E7] and negative ROE of -0.59% [E8], which demonstrate that the company is currently destroying shareholder value rather than generating it. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 0.04x [E1]. However, this extreme discount is not a sign of hidden value but a reflection of a business that has failed to produce a dividend [E3] and has seen its 5-year profit growth collapse by -36% [E14]. The bull’s claim that the market is failing to appreciate the company is refuted by the price-led signal [E45], which indicates that investor expectations are already running 77% ahead of actual delivery. Finally, the stock’s position at the very bottom of its 52-week range [E4] confirms that the market has priced in the persistent long-term stagnation evidenced by a 10-year profit growth rate of only 2% [E13].
